9.title: Surah Al-Fatihah (The Opening) - Complete
9.translationMaulana: All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, the Beneficent, the Merciful, Master of the Day of Judgment. Thee alone do we worship and Thee alone do we ask for help. Guide us on the right path, the path of those upon whom Thou hast bestowed favors. Not those upon whom Thy wrath is brought down, nor those who go astray.
9.translationYusuf: Praise be to Allah, the Cherisher and Sustainer of the worlds; Most Gracious, Most Merciful; Master of the Day of Judgment. Thee do we worship, and Thine aid we seek. Show us the straight way, the way of those on whom Thou hast bestowed Thy Grace, those whose portion is not wrath, and who go not astray.
9.transliteration: Al-hamdu lillahi rabbi al-alameen. Ar-Rahman ar-Rahim. Maliki yawmi ad-din. Iyyaka na'abudu wa iyyaka nasta'een. Ihdina as-sirat al-mustaqeem. Sirat alladhina an'amta alayhim ghayri al-maghdubi alayhim wa la ad-dalleen.
9.annotations: Surah 1, Verses 1-7: The Opening Chapter recited in every Islamic prayer unit.
9.context: Al-Fatihah is the introduction to the Quran, establishing core Islamic beliefs in divine oneness and human submission.

10.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:1-2:5)
10.translationMaulana: Alif. Lam. Meem. This is the Book; in it is guidance sure, without doubt, to those who fear Allah; Who believe in the Unseen, are steadfast in prayer, and spend out of what We have provided for them.
10.translationYusuf: Alif. Lam. Meem. This is the Book; in it is guidance sure, without doubt, to those who fear Allah. Those who believe in the Unseen, establish regular Prayer, and spend (in Charity) out of what We have provided for them.
10.transliteration: Alif. Lam. Meem. Dhalika al-kitab la rayba fih hudal lil-muttaqeen.
10.annotations: Surah 2, Verses 1-5: The longest chapter of the Quran begins with mysterious letters.
10.context: Al-Baqarah (The Cow) opens with guidance for the God-conscious.

11.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:6-2:20)
11.translationMaulana: As to those who reject Faith, it is the same to them whether thou warn them or not; they will not believe. Allah hath sealed up their hearts and their hearing, and on their eyes is a veil...
11.translationYusuf: As to those who reject Faith, it is the same to them whether thou warn them or not; they will not believe. Allah hath set a seal on their hearts and on their hearing, and on their eyes is a veil...
11.transliteration: Inna alladhina kafaroo sawaa alayhim a'andhartahum am lam tundhirhum la yu'minoon.
11.annotations: Surah 2, Verses 6-20: Description of those who reject faith and hypocrites.
11.context: Continued narrative of Al-Baqarah regarding believers and disbelievers.

12.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:21-2:39)
12.translationMaulana: O ye people! Worship your Guardian-Lord, who created you and those who came before you, that ye may have the chance to learn righteousness...
12.translationYusuf: O ye people! Worship your Guardian-Lord, Who created you and those who came before you, that ye may have the chance to learn righteousness...
12.transliteration: Ya ayyuha an-nasu o'bodu rabbakum alladhee khalaqakum...
12.annotations: Surah 2, Verses 21-39: Call to worship Allah and story of Adam.
12.context: Quranic teaching on divine worship and human creation.

13.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:40-2:59)
13.translationMaulana: O Children of Israel! Call to mind the favor which I bestowed upon you, and that I preferred you to all other for My Message and My Signs...
13.translationYusuf: O Children of Israel! Call to mind the favor which I bestowed upon you, and that I preferred you to all nations for My Message and My Signs...
13.transliteration: Ya bani isra'eela udhkuroo ni'mati allatee an'amtu alaykum...
13.annotations: Surah 2, Verses 40-59: Message to Children of Israel and the Exodus.
13.context: Historical narrative of Allah's favor upon the Israelites.

14.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:60-2:82)
14.translationMaulana: And remember, We divided the sea for you and saved you and drowned Pharaoh's people within your very sight. And remember We appointed forty nights for Moses...
14.translationYusuf: And remember We divided the sea for you and saved you and drowned Pharaoh's people within your very sight. And remember We appointed forty nights for Moses...
14.transliteration: Wa idh faragalna bikum al-bahra fa-anjaynak wa aghraqna ala fir'awna...
14.annotations: Surah 2, Verses 60-82: Divine miracles and covenant with Children of Israel.
14.context: Continuation of stories of Moses and the Israelites.

15.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:83-2:104)
15.translationMaulana: And remember We took a Covenant from the Children of Israel: Worship none but Allah; treat with kindness your parents and kindred...
15.translationYusuf: And remember We took a Covenant from the Children of Israel: Worship none but Allah; treat with kindness your parents and kindred...
15.transliteration: Wa idh akhdhana miithaaqa bani isra'eela la ta'budoona illa allah...
15.annotations: Surah 2, Verses 83-104: Covenant and commandments for Children of Israel.
15.context: Divine commandments regarding worship and ethical conduct.

16.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:105-2:123)
16.translationMaulana: Neither those who reject Faith among the People of the Book nor the Pagans wish that any good should come down to you from your Lord...
16.translationYusuf: Neither those who reject Faith among the People of the Book nor the Pagans wish that any good should come down to you from your Lord...
16.transliteration: Ma yawoddoo alladhina kafaroo min ahli al-kitaab wa la al-mushrikoon...
16.annotations: Surah 2, Verses 105-123: Addressing divisions between communities.
16.context: Quranic guidance on religious differences and unity.

17.title: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:124-2:141) - END of JUZ 1
17.translationMaulana: Remember that Abraham was tried by his Lord with certain Commands, which he fulfilled: He said: I will make thee an Imam to the Nations. He pleaded: And also (Imams) from my offspring! He answered: But My Promise is not within the reach of evil-doers.
17.translationYusuf: Remember that Abraham was tried by his Lord with certain commands which he fulfilled: He said: I will make thee an Imam to the Nations. He pleaded: And also (Imams) from my offspring! He answered: But My Promise is not within the reach of evil-doers.
17.transliteration: Wa idh ibtala ibrahima rabbihu bi-kalimatin fa-atammahunna...
17.annotations: Surah 2, Verses 124-141: Story of Abraham and covenant of faith. FINAL VERSES OF JUZ 1.
17.context: Conclusion of the first section of the Quran with Abraham's covenant and faith of believers.
